subject: Transportation Systems
title: Dedicated vs. Shared Track
description: A 60-second lesson on Dedicated vs. Shared Track.

hook.text: A high-speed train on freight tracks is just a regular train stuck behind cargo. Track matters.

buildup.text: Dedicated high-speed lines have gentle curves, no level crossings, and no freight interference.

discovery.text: Building dedicated track costs $25 to $80 million per mile, depending on terrain and land prices.

twist.text: Some countries use shared track to save money but sacrifice top speed. Germany does this extensively.

climax.text: Japan and France invested in fully dedicated lines. Their trains run faster and more reliably.

punchline.text: Shared tracks save money. Dedicated tracks deliver speed.

quiz.question: Why do dedicated high-speed lines outperform shared track?
options: No freight delays, gentle curves, and no level crossings
